prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment, disinfection, storage to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (alias Ironwood): auto start per demand/channel depth; permissives suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; start blocked on low channel level, drive fault, local control, unproven interlock; lost permissive -> alarm/stop. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot each cleaning cycle end; high-high level needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (alias Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket on new lot (Lab Technician uses it to verify lot identity); dose trim from verified analyzer feedback, not single instrument. North Filter Gallery (alias Cobalt): records turbidity/headloss each scan. South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note when run ends outside limits. Filter return only after rinse-to-waste meets target. Chlorine Contact Basin. Clearwell Level Controller: coordinated with filter production. Backwash Recovery Tank: sampled after return-to-process events. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (alias Sparrow): custody-controlled receipt; sends Jar Test Photograph Set after date/time/ID check. High Service Pump Header. SCADA Historian Server (alias Lantern): time-sync master; retains trends, doses, analyzer values, filter status, washes, comments, accepted lab result timestamps with trend interval for audit. Actors: Chief Operator (modes, targets, Storm Intake Mode, starting dose, approves large manual corrections, trend review, sampling priorities; notified when lab doesn't support field indication behind adjustment); Duty Engineer (reviews significant field/lab differences affecting feed, filters, disinfection); Laboratory Technician (checks container, holding time, temperature, preservative, seal; sends Sample Chain Slip after custody entries complete/legible; records label/log/note mismatches before acceptance; turbidity and residual method checks; preserves custody/acceptance records for Chief Operator, Duty Engineer, regulatory auditors); Maintenance Planner; Distribution Dispatcher; Chemical Supplier Driver; Residuals Hauler; North/South Distribution Pressure Station. Chlorine Residual Alarm: high priority; related grab samples prioritized. Modes: Automatic; Manual override (only when auto unavailable; state reason, monitor, restore ASAP, small increments); Reduced-capacity; Storm Intake Mode (increase sampling until raw/settled stable); return to normal when stable. Analyzer loss -> hold last verified safe/approved fixed dose plus grab samples. Field readings

Document units:
S101: Planned maintenance is controlled through a work order process that ties each task to an approved operating window, a named responsible person, and a defined return-to-service condition.
S102: The Chief Operator reviews the next-day schedule with operations staff so that treatment capacity, water quality risk, and distribution demand are understood before work is released.
S103: The Maintenance Planner is also known as Quarry for internal radio coordination during maintenance planning discussions.
S104: The Maintenance Planner verifies that each work order identifies affected equipment, required isolations, parts staging, and the evidence needed to close the work.
S105: The Maintenance Planner uses the snapshot to compare planned rake work against recent mechanical loading before releasing the task package.
S106: The Duty Engineer checks proposed work against current operating constraints and may defer nonessential activity when treatment margin is limited.
S107: Lockout planning identifies electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical, and stored-energy hazards before personnel enter or service plant equipment.
S108: Field isolation is verified locally by the assigned craft worker and then acknowledged by operations before the equipment is opened, adjusted, or tested.
S109: Ironwood shall remain unavailable for routine maintenance release until isolation points are tagged, verified locally, and acknowledged in the shift turnover record.
S110: Work in the North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery is scheduled to keep enough filtration capacity available for expected demand and wash cycles.
S111: Any planned change affecting the Clearwell Level Controller requires coordination with the High Service Pump Header operating plan before the change is applied.
S112: The Chemical Supplier Driver sends the Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading any replacement cylinders at the plant.
S113: Supplier access is limited to approved routes, assigned unloading areas, and times when an operator is available to observe chemical connections and vehicle movement.
S114: Deliveries for the Coagulant Dosing Skid are staged so that hoses, containment, and emergency washdown equipment are inspected before transfer begins.
S115: Chemical work near the Chlorine Contact Basin is coordinated with operating staff so that ventilation, gas monitoring, and communications are available during the task.
S116: Shift communication includes the status of open isolations, temporary operating limits, unavailable equipment, and any abnormal condition that could affect the next crew.
S117: The Distribution Dispatcher is informed before maintenance changes the availability of the High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station.
